mft_h264.note: The H.264 encoder Media Foundation transform (M15.11). register true: the installer copies payload/mft/amdgpu_wddm_mft_h264.dll to <install root>\mft\ and writes route A of driver/umd/mft-h264/INSTALL.md machine wide. register false: the installer installs and registers nothing, and takes away what an earlier install of this release family wrote. The value travels into manifest.json, so the package itself says what it does. This is the bisect lever of the encoder wagon.

public_commits.note: Built commit -> commit on a public branch, for every pair that differs. The b19 part of this release is published: D-Ogi/amdgpu-wddm holds 85ac47b6 and 3ef45a0f on branch train/b19-setup, and D-Ogi/mesa-amdgpu-wddm holds 31844893 on amdgpu-wddm/b19-icd, 76ab2c27 on amdgpu-wddm/b19-desktop-umd and 7117b189 on amdgpu-wddm/b19-hosted-umd. D-Ogi/dxvk, D-Ogi/vkd3d-proton and D-Ogi/dxil-spirv keep branch amdgpu-wddm/upstream-2026-10-05. The system Vulkan ICD is the build of 2732f9c8, which the fork publishes on branch amdgpu-wddm/gdi-immediate-quiet (597fc6e2), as in 0.7.205.100-tester.11. The hosted ICD of the desktop route is the build of 48546c73. The b20 part is NOT published yet. One commit of bc250-win branch train/b20-setup built every rebuilt file of this respin: bc1b00a9, the head of the respin (the release notes of 0.7.213.100-tester.15). Its working tree held one uncommitted file while the builds ran, this manifest itself, which is no source of any binary. Four later commits of the branch touch no binary of this package. f457ff5f changes the lab overlay's absent-value table (tools/win/bc250mon, which the release does not install) and 1897bdd6 changes a release gate. The review pass is two commits: 88d60534 rewrites RELEASE-NOTES.md, three documents, one comment of driver/kmd/wddm.c and one lab script, and c4b05b61 makes the kernel recipe delete the debug information of an earlier build with its objects, so that the driver reproduces in a directory that already holds a build and not only in an empty one. The package is assembled at c4b05b61, so its RELEASE-NOTES.md is that commit's. The kernel driver was rebuilt at both commits and gave the same bytes, and so did the control application, its DLL and the CLI, which is how this manifest knows that neither commit changes a binary. The H.264 transform and the two caps records are not rebuilt: the transform is the tester.14 build of 689852a8, and the records are byte for byte the b19 ones, because b20 reuses the b19 engines and ICDs. Push train/b20-setup to D-Ogi/amdgpu-wddm before this release goes to a tester. Each b20 wagon is an ancestor of the branch head: train/b19-repro-kmd edae6987, kmd209-iflip2 b03da3a7, fan/read-nct6686 9d1aff7c, c48/notifydpc-in-report 677709c2, tuner/vf-cpu dabdd949, m15/router-iflip-front 99ba8cd8, bd075/capshare-trace 3325c555, bd075/d3d12-shared-real 1fa1cfb6, e52/encoder-perf e4d1f630, dpm/thermal-soft-zone 846ad919, kmd/confirm-soft 01cee34c, m14/d3d11-iflip2 0b325308 and m15/d3d12-iflip2 ef63bab3, on main af76883c. Three files come from a build of a b19 wagon, not from a b20 commit: payload/syswow64/bc250umd.dll from train/b19-wow64-x86 a748e78e, and the two desktop CPU and hosted UMDs from their Mesa branches. The x86 patches of the earlier releases are gone (BD-064). Both b19 RADV files report git-3184489333 as their Mesa version, which is 31844893. 0.7.213.101-tester.16 is tester.15 with one file rebuilt: payload/desktop/bc250d3d_zink.dll, from D-Ogi/mesa-amdgpu-wddm 7eb7861d on amdgpu-wddm/b19-hosted-umd (pushed), built by scratch/train/b20-build/umd-fix/build-zink.ps1 with the b19 recipe; its host test passed.

files.role: KMD 0.7.213.1 INF (bc250-win bc1b00a9, train/b20-setup). It writes the four Parameters values of this train's finished features: EnableHwmon 1, HwmonBasePort 0, EnableDirectFlipHandshake 1 and NotifyDpcInReport 1. Each of the three ones is a feature that rides on, with 0 as its bisect switch. The release re-stamps DriverVer and adds the Reboot directive

KMD 0.7.213.1, escape ABI 0x000700D5 (bc250-win c4b05b61, train/b20-setup: main af76883c with the seven b20 kernel wagons). The kernel is built with /Brepro and a sorted object list, and five builds into clean directories gave the same unsigned bytes: two of bc1b00a9 and one each of the three commits of this branch above it. Seven changes against 0.7.208.1, and the four that a tester meets are on by every install, each with one Parameters value that takes it away again. The driver can hand its own swap-chain buffers to the scan-out hardware and publishes the scan-out caps trailer that the D3D11 and the D3D12 shell read (route C increment 2, EnableDirectFlipHandshake; the compositor's own user-mode driver, the router front, does not query it yet and still answers the DirectFlip question FALSE). It reads the fan speed, the fan duty and its own temperatures from the Super I/O chip, and only reads them (EnableHwmon). It pairs the notification of a finished packet with the report pass itself (NotifyDpcInReport), and it keeps a histogram of the gap between the ring and the vertical blank. The clock governor steps the cap down inside a soft thermal zone below the 87 C hot limit, with a lead measured over a fixed slope window (DpmThermalZone). CONFIRM and the CPU KEEP operation no longer suspend the GPU scheduler: both answer with NoAdapterSynchronization, and both still admit the old HardwareAccess word for one release. The operator can give the automatic clock a voltage curve of their own, and can set a clock limit, an undervolt and a temperature cap for the processor, each one as a trial that falls back by itself. Re-signed with the release certificate, code unchanged
UMD stub, D3D9 slot of UserModeDriverName (driver/umd-stub)

D3D12 shell (bc250-win bc1b00a9, train/b20-setup). It sizes its adapter query BC250_SCANOUT_CAPS_TOTAL, so it reaches the kernel's scan-out caps trailer and reads the new scan-out counters; its E26R record is still 16 bytes of version 2, which the compositor's 64-byte version 3 opener refuses, so the D3D12 client half of route C increment 2 is open (M15.14). It makes a shared texture inside a known shape instead of refusing it, and it counts every second create attempt (BD-075). A command queue accepts a wait on a fence and lets the system do the waiting, where the shell before this one lost the device. Every earlier behaviour of the b19 shell is kept: heap import retries the ownership unlock (BD-045), ClearRootArguments records the real values (BD-046), the direct recording entry of engine-ddi is the default (M15.9), and the shell records each start of an application for the Recent page. Built with /Brepro

D3D12 engine (vkd3d-proton fork amdgpu-wddm/upstream-2026-10-05 4e9a98e9: 16 upstream commits merged into the b17 compile limiter 220099f5, submodule dxil-spirv d2d82332 = 14 upstream commits merged into bc773cf2)

D3D12 ICD (mesa fork amdgpu-wddm/b19-icd 31844893 on upstream-2026-10-05). The shader cache key covers the whole shader state again (BD-068). Handle types and host imports follow the contract (BD-038, BD-039). A buffer object takes the CPU lock for a mapped import (BD-045). Host policy version 2 reads no machine-wide file and writes no shared log. The disk cache stays one file. The file reports git-3184489333 as its Mesa version

desktop and application router (bc250-win bc1b00a9, train/b20-setup, driver/umd/router). gpu-default keeps Windows components and unresolved images on the CPU UMD, as in b19. The router carries the Direct3D 11.1 front of route C (M15.14), and from this release the front is installed by default: an absent DirectFlipFront means on, 0 is its bisect switch and leaves the shipped router in place, and a value of the wrong type is refused and reported

hosted zink D3D11 UMD for DWM on the GPU (mesa fork amdgpu-wddm/b19-hosted-umd 7eb7861d). The surface setup resumes after a failed step instead of leaking it (BD-037). The composed-surface table accepts one-byte pixels (A8). The shader parser reads past the extended operand token (the minimum-precision hint) that the Direct3D 11.1 front of route C passes on, and the adapter sets the CRT error mode to stderr, so a failed assertion ends the process instead of a message box that nobody sees (BD-088, the b20 logon hang)
hosted ICD for zink

CPU D3D11 UMD (mesa fork amdgpu-wddm/b19-desktop-umd 76ab2c27). The surface setup resumes after a failed step instead of leaking it (BD-037). The composed-surface table accepts one-byte pixels (A8). This is the fallback route for the D3D11 applications that the router does not send to the GPU

GPU D3D11 shell (bc250-win bc1b00a9, train/b20-setup). It sizes its adapter caps query BC250_SCANOUT_CAPS_TOTAL, the last trailer of driver/contract, so that it reaches the kernel's scan-out caps trailer at all (route C increment 2). The 11 host tests of the recipe and the DDI error-policy gate pass against it. Built with /Brepro against DXVK fork 5611118e, which b20 reuses from b19 unchanged

GPU D3D11 caps record for engine C242BA6A and ICD 822134D0 (tools/build/write-umd-config.py). The shell refuses an engine or an ICD whose SHA-256 differs from this record. b20 reuses the b19 engine and ICD, so this record is byte for byte the b19 one. Capabilities carried from fl12caps001: FL 12_1, tiled resources tier 3, rasterizer ordered views, conservative rasterization tier 3

GPU D3D11 engine (DXVK fork amdgpu-wddm/upstream-2026-10-05 5611118e: 14 upstream commits merged into the b17 inline-throttle engine ebeadc49, the throttle wait moved to the new upstream wait site, plus the signal-tracker deduplication fix; submodule dxbc-spirv stays at f241996e)

system Vulkan ICD (mesa fork 2732f9c8, published on branch amdgpu-wddm/gdi-immediate-quiet, the build the lab registers). b19 keeps it. The b19 ICD 822134D0 is newer. Its branch does not carry the work of this build: the IMMEDIATE present on the GDI path without the DwmFlush wait, and host-cached present memory. That work has to come onto the b19 ICD line before the system ICD can move. docs/testing/defaults-audit-2026-10-04.md row 6 names what this build costs: no shader disk cache, and no ICD change after 2026-09-27

H.264 encoder Media Foundation transform (bc250-win 689852a8, train/b20-setup, which carries e52/encoder-perf e4d1f630). The respin does not rebuild it: no commit of the respin touches driver/umd/mft-h264 or the contract headers it includes, so this is the file the tester.14 build staged, and the lab kit of E52 pins it. The encoder holds two pictures at once, it filters a whole picture in one dispatch, and its rate control reads the quantiser the content needs. A client that asks for low latency still gets one picture at a time. BC250_MFT_DEPTH=1, BC250_MFT_DEBLOCK=waves and BC250_MFT_SERIAL_DEBLOCK each select an older part. The conformance sweep is 76 of 76, and 60 of 60 pictures stay bit exact against the inbox decoder. The build matches the hash the wagon recorded
